name: add_dependency
description:
Records that one component depends on another.

Components are authored as records (3aeb66cf), and their dependencies with
them. Until this tool an edge could only arrive by a spec file's
`## Dependencies` being synced, so an architecture designed through the tools
had no way to say what depended on what.

source_component_id.description: The component that depends on the other

name: architecture_health_summary
description:
Provides a comprehensive health overview of the system architecture including:
- Story coverage: assigned/unassigned component counts
- Context distribution: components grouped by story count (1, 2-6, 7+)
- Dependency issues: missing references, high fan-out contexts
- Data quality: duplicate stories and other consistency issues

This gives LLMs and developers a quick health assessment of the entire architecture.

name: context_statistics
description:
Provides statistical overview of each component context including:
- Story count per component
- Dependency in/out counts per component
- Results sorted by story count or dependency count
- Raw numbers for LLM analysis

name: create_component
description:
Creates a single component, as a record marked `:authored`.

The patch-mode alternative to rewriting the full architecture proposal: the
architect adds one component at a time during incremental design. It used to
write a stub spec file too, which was then the only way the component's
dependencies could be recorded; `add_dependency` does that now, and no file
is written (3aeb66cf, step 2).

type.description: Component type: context, coordination_context, live_context, schema, behaviour, json, liveview, liveview_component, controller, module, infrastructure.

name: delete_component
description:
Deletes a component. Its files are left alone; while live code still names
the module, the next sync discovers it again.

name: get_component
description:
One component as its record describes it: type, description, provenance,
parent, what it depends on (each marked planned and/or in code) and the
files that belong to it. By id or by module name. Components are records
(3aeb66cf); this is how an agent reads one without listing the whole
architecture.

module_name.description: Or its module name, e.g. MyApp.Accounts.

name: list_components
description: Lists all components in a project

name: orphaned_contexts
description: Lists all contexts with no user story and no dependencies

name: remove_dependency
description:
Removes one component's dependency on another. The other half of
`AddDependency`.

source_component_id.description: The component that depends on the other

target_component_id.description: The component it should no longer depend on

name: review_context_design
description: Reviews current context design against best practices and provides architectural feedback

name: show_architecture
description:
Renders the project's component dependency graph as a Mermaid flowchart.

Returns plain text — a `flowchart TD` followed by node and edge lines for
every context, liveview, live_context, controller, and channel in the
project. Dependencies declared on child components are rolled up to the
containing surface, so the graph stays at the architecture level the
architect cares about, not raw module-to-module.

Mermaid was picked over JSON for two reasons: it's far less verbose for
the same information, and it renders directly in any markdown-aware
reader the agent or human is using.

name: update_component
description:
Updates a component.
Include all fields in the input that you want to update.
They will be persisted exactly as you send them.

parent_component_id.description: The component this one belongs under, e.g. its context
